evals.prompt: Add a new password reset endpoint to the fixture project. Follow the closest existing endpoint exactly where the conventions match, and explain any deliberate divergence.
evals.expected_output: A password reset endpoint that mirrors the existing endpoint's location, naming, imports, response shape, and test style, with divergences called out.
assertions: The response identifies getUser.ts as the reference
The proposed file stays under src/users
The endpoint uses the existing async handler and response conventions
The response includes a matching test or explains why one is not added
Any difference from the reference is explicitly labeled as a divergence

evals.prompt: Add a listUsers function to the fixture project. Match the neighboring getUser function and its test conventions rather than introducing a new abstraction.
evals.expected_output: A listUsers implementation and test that reuse the neighboring module's structure without adding unnecessary layers.
assertions: The response names the neighboring getUser function as the reference
The new function follows the same import and export style
The response proposes a test in the same test location and style
The response does not introduce a service, class, or dispatcher without evidence
The response distinguishes copied conventions from task-specific changes

evals.prompt: Add an audit export module to the fixture project. There is no existing export module, so inspect the available conventions and state where you must choose a new one.
evals.expected_output: A proposed module grounded in nearby project conventions that clearly identifies decisions with no existing analog.
assertions: The response inspects or cites the available neighboring conventions
The response proposes a concrete location and naming convention
The response explicitly flags the missing export analog as a divergence or new convention
The response avoids claiming that an export pattern exists when it does not
